The Benue State Police Command has arrested a man found in possession of a pistol during the All Progressives Congress campaign flag-off in Gboko, Benue State. The spokesperson for the state command, DSP Peter Aondongu, disclosed this in a statement issued and made available to journalists in Makurdi on Wednesday. According to the police spokesman, a Beretta pistol was recovered from the suspect, identified as Saalu Fidelis Teryange, during security screening at the venue of the campaign rally last Thursday. He warned politicians in the state against instigating violence during the ongoing political activities, adding that the command would not tolerate any attempt by individuals or groups to use the electioneering period as an opportunity to foment trouble, engage in political thuggery, intimidate opponents or undermine the peace and security of the state. The statement read in part, “The warning follows the arrest of a male suspect, identified as Saalu Fidelis Teryange, during security screening at a political campaign event held at J.S. Tarka Stadium, Gboko, on Thursday, 19th November 2026. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. N. Nwadiogbu, psc(+), mnips, PhD, alongside the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations, were physically present to supervise the security arrangements which paid off with the arrest and recovery of the lethal weapon.” The command spokesperson reaffirmed the command’s commitment to maintaining peace and security throughout the ongoing electioneering period. According to him, the state Commissioner of Police had directed Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and Tactical Commanders to sustain heightened vigilance, strengthen intelligence-led policing and ensure adequate security coverage of political gatherings and other public events across the state. The command assured residents of its readiness to discharge its constitutional responsibility of protecting lives and property before, during and after the electioneering period. He charged members of the public to remain law-abiding and promptly report suspicious movements or activities to the nearest police station. John Charles
